title: Auto Repair Cost Per Lead 2026: Google, LSA and Facebook
summary: Auto repair shop clicks cost $4.21 to $7.41 on average in the US. See cost per lead at 5%, 10% and 15% conversion, plus Google vs LSA vs Facebook.
body_markdown:
## The short answer


- A click on the main auto repair searches in the US averages $4.21 to $7.41, and top-of-page bids run from $2.01 to $9.84 depending on the search.
- At the $4.21 average for 'auto repair', a 10% conversion rate gives a lead for about $42 ($4.21 / 0.10 = $42.10). At 5% it is $84, and at 15% it is $28.
- On Facebook and Instagram, LocaliQ's 2026 all-industry figure is $27.39 per lead, against $66.69 for all-industry Google search. Meta leads come from people who were not searching, so judge them by booked jobs.
- A sensible starting budget is jobs wanted / booking rate x cost per lead. Twenty jobs at 1 booked in 3 leads and $42 a lead is $2,520 a month.


## What a click costs


These are the four searches most auto repair shops bid on. The prices are US figures for a click at the top of Google.


Keyword Searches a month (US) Average CPC Top-of-page range


auto repair 301,000 $4.21 $2.47 to $9.63


car repair near me 165,000 $5.63 $2.09 to $8.81


mechanic near me 673,000 $6.15 $2.01 to $8.69


brake repair 135,000 $7.41 $2.64 to $9.84


The spread is wide because three things move the price. Urgency pushes it up: a driver with a grinding brake pedal will call the first shop that answers, so shops bid hard for 'brake repair'. Competition matters too, since more shops bidding in the same city means a higher price for the same click. City is the third factor, because a dense metro area costs more per click than a small town, and the gap between the low and high end of each range is largely a gap between those markets.


## From click to cost per lead


A click is not a lead. Cost per lead is your cost per click divided by the share of clicks that turn into a call or a form. The table uses the $4.21 average for 'auto repair'. The booked-job column is an example: say 1 in 3 leads books a job.


Conversion rate Cost per lead Cost per booked job (1 in 3 books)


5% $84 ($4.21 / 0.05 = $84.20) $253 ($84.20 x 3 = $252.60)


10% $42 ($4.21 / 0.10 = $42.10) $126 ($42.10 x 3 = $126.30)


15% $28 ($4.21 / 0.15 = $28.07) $84 ($28.07 x 3 = $84.21)


The conversion rate is the lever you control most. Going from 5% to 15% cuts the cost per lead to a third without changing the click price. To try your own click price, conversion rate and booking rate, use the[cost per lead calculator](https://www.sprites.ai/tools/cost-per-lead-calculator) .


## Google Ads vs Local Services Ads vs Facebook for auto repair shops


Google Ads (Search) Local Services Ads Facebook and Instagram


How you pay Per click, set by auction Per lead, with the price set by Google by category and area Per impression or click, often optimized for a lead form


Intent High. The driver is searching for a fix now High. The driver is looking for a local provider and often calls Lower. The person was scrolling, not searching


When it wins for this trade Urgent jobs such as brakes, a check engine light or a car that will not start When it is offered for your category and area, and you can answer calls quickly, because you pay only for the lead Planned work and standing offers, such as maintenance or inspections, and reaching nearby drivers before they need you


Local Services Ads are priced by Google, so there is no number to quote here. Whether LSA is offered for auto repair depends on your category and area, so check your Google Ads account for what is available and what it quotes. Our guide to[Google Local Services Ads](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/google-local-services-ads) covers how the program works.


For benchmarks, LocaliQ's 2026 figures for Automotive: Repair, Service & Parts show a Google search cost per lead of $29.96, an average click price of $4.35 and a conversion rate of 15.51%. LocaliQ's 2026 all-industry figures are $66.69 per lead on Google search and $27.39 per lead on Meta. The all-industry numbers are not specific to auto repair shops, and a Meta lead is a different kind of lead from a search call. See the[average cost per lead by industry](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/average-cost-per-lead-by-industry) for more comparisons.


## How much to spend each month


Work backward from the jobs you want:


1. Pick the number of booked jobs you want from ads each month.
2. Divide by your booking rate to get the leads you need.
3. Multiply the leads by your cost per lead.


In one line: monthly budget = jobs wanted / booking rate x cost per lead.


Here is a worked example with stated inputs. Say you want 20 booked jobs a month, 1 in 3 leads books, and your cost per lead is $42 (a $4.21 click at a 10% conversion rate). You need 20 / (1/3) = 60 leads, and 60 x $42 = $2,520 a month. If you reached LocaliQ's 2026 Automotive: Repair, Service & Parts figure of $29.96 per lead, the same 60 leads would cost 60 x $29.96 = $1,797.60.


Start on one channel, usually Google Search for urgent repairs, and run it long enough to learn your real conversion and booking rates before you add another. Our[Google Ads cost guide](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/google-ads-cost) goes deeper on budgets, and the[auto shop marketing guide](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/auto-body-marketing) covers the wider picture beyond paid ads.


## How to lower your cost per lead


- **Make one clear offer.** A brake inspection or a diagnostic visit gives a driver a reason to call you first. Put it in the headline and the first line of the ad.
- **Send each search to a matching page.** Someone searching 'brake repair' should land on a brake page with your phone number, hours, address and reviews at the top, not on a general home page.
- **Answer the phone.** Most repair leads call, and a missed call at $7.41 a click is money gone. Show ads when someone can pick up, and track calls so you know which searches produce them.
- **Add negative keywords.** Block searches like 'jobs', 'salary', 'parts', 'how to', 'diy', 'school' and 'free' so you stop paying for people who are not buying a repair.
- **Tighten your service area.** Target a radius you can actually serve and name your towns in the ad copy. Clicks from drivers too far away to drop off a car are wasted.
- **Keep the lead form short.** Ask for name, phone, vehicle make and model, and the problem. Every extra field lowers the conversion rate, which raises your cost per lead.


For ideas on copy and creative, see what auto repair shops run on Facebook in the[auto repair ad examples](https://www.sprites.ai/auto-repair-ads) .
